text.brief: In September 1821 a woman selling fruit from a boat beside the American ship Emily at Whampoa fell into the river and drowned. Qing officials charged a sailor named Francis Terranova with striking her with an earthenware jar.
text.record: The American merchants tried Terranova aboard ship and refused to hand him over. Qing officials stopped all American trade until they did. The merchants surrendered him, a Qing court convicted him, and officials executed him by strangulation in October 1821.
text.reading: The Qing court proved that trade access could buy a person, and the merchants proved that a guest with no law of its own will pay. The episode fed the American demand for extraterritoriality that Caleb Cushing won in 1844.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. No American authority held the jurisdiction question, so each merchant weighed his cargo against one sailor's life.
text.fix: Settle jurisdiction and consular access by treaty before the incident, so no trade lever can buy a citizen.
